12. A function f is even if /(x) = /(—x) and odd if /(x) = —/(—x). For 
example, f is even if /(x) = x2 or /(x) = |x| or f(x) = cosx, while f is
odd if /(x) = x or /(x) = sinx.
(a) Determine whether f + g is even, odd, or not necessarily either, in the
four cases obtained by choosing f even or odd, and g even or odd. (Your
answers can most conveniently be displayed in a 2 x 2 table.)
(b) Do the same for f • g.
(c) Do the same for fog.
(d) Prove that every even function f can be written /(x) = g(|x|), for infinitely many functions g.

(b) Prove that this way of writing f is unique. (If you try to do part (b) first,
by “solving” for E and O you will probably find the solution to part (a).)
